title: WarcraftXL mod manifest
description: Sits next to a mod's binaries as mod.json. Read before anything of the mod runs, so that a mod whose needs cannot be met is refused with a readable reason rather than failing on its first call.

id.description: Stable identity, unique across every mod. Also what wxl_mod_info.id reports, and what other mods name in loadAfter.

abi.description: The lowest contract version the mod needs, major.minor.feature, e.g. "0.1.5". A runtime refuses a different major; while the major is 0, a different minor; and within the same major.minor, a feature higher than its own. A binary must be built against headers of this major.minor and at least this feature. A Lua mod may use only what this version has: subscribing to an event a later feature brought is refused.

binaries.description: One binary per target, by platform and architecture. A runtime loads the entry matching its own; a mod with no entry for it is skipped, not failed. A script mod leaves it out and names "lua" instead: a manifest has one or the other, never both.

additionalProperties.description: Path to the binary, relative to the mod folder.

requires.description: Services the mod cannot run without. A runtime missing one refuses the mod before it loads and says which.

optional.description: Services the mod uses when they are there. Declared so that a runtime can report what a mod will do without, rather than leaving it silent.

loadAfter.description: Mod ids to load before this one, when they are present. Not a dependency: a missing id is ignored.

lua.description: The Lua entry file, relative to the mod folder, run by wxl.lua in a state of its own. A manifest with "lua" is a script mod: the same folder runs on every runtime, with nothing to build. It names no "binaries": a manifest with both is refused.

net.description: The messages of the world connection the mod speaks (wxl.net). Read before any of the mod's code runs: a number another mod loaded earlier declares refuses this one.

opcodes.description: The opcode numbers the mod claims, each a number, a string "0x521", or a range "0x521-0x52A". A mod that declares numbers can claim only these; another mod cannot claim them at all. Numbers up to 0x520 are the client's own and need "stock".

stock.description: Lets the mod claim and send the client's own opcode numbers (up to 0x520). For tools; a game mod never needs it. Observing the client's own traffic through MessageReceived needs nothing.

service.description: The name the service is published under, e.g. "wxl.object".

version.description: The exact version required. A different published version does not match.
